note: Human adjudications of QI-v2 questions that appear in more than one recurrence family. This file is HAND-MAINTAINED and is an INPUT to build_historical_qi_inventory.py -- never edit docs/study/historical_qi_asset_inventory.json directly. The builder FAILS CLOSED: a shared question with no entry here, or an entry whose `families` no longer matches what the QI-v2 ref actually holds, stops the build rather than shipping an unexplained double membership.
authority: MIW study adjudication. It classifies an EXISTING relationship between existing families; it never renames, merges, splits or deletes a family. Family identity lives on the QI-v2 research ref and is read-only to this layer.
why_this_exists: The QI-v2 limb model states that recurrence is observed at LIMB level. A question is therefore ALLOWED to belong to more than one family, because its limbs can. The join builder could only see question ids, so it reported every double membership as a suspected defect. This file supplies the limb dimension the join could not see.

verdicts.LEGITIMATE_MULTI_FAMILY: The memberships are real and must both stand. Separate limbs, or a limb and its parent whole question, genuinely belong to separate families.
verdicts.ONE_FAMILY_PRIMARY_ONE_SUPPORTING: Both memberships are real but one is subordinate; the supporting family must never be quoted as independent evidence.
verdicts.DUPLICATE_FAMILY_DEFECT: The same family was serialised twice. Resolve by the governed supersession pattern, never by deletion.
verdicts.WRONG_OCCURRENCE_ASSIGNMENT: An occurrence record names the wrong parent question. Repair the occurrence, not the family.
verdicts.REQUIRES_MORE_SOURCE_EVIDENCE: Cannot be settled from held sources. Stays flagged.

membership_kinds.DISJOINT_LIMBS: The two families attach to two DIFFERENT limbs of the same question. Neither limb evidences the other.
membership_kinds.LIMB_WITHIN_WHOLE_QUESTION: One family tracks a single limb across sittings; the other tracks the whole question against its ancestor. Nested, not duplicate -- and the limb's sitting count must never be read as the whole question's.
